Throughput is NOT the confound: MFU came in at 43.38%, the highest in the cell so far (above a5's 41.9% at depth 10), so the grad_accum 2->4 handicap I flagged before the run never materialised. The model is simply starved: 200.9M params trained on 125.3M tokens in 478 steps, i.e. ~0.6 tokens per parameter, versus 85.9M params on 293M tokens (~3.4 tok/param) at depth 10. Reading depth 8 (~0.997 at 2^18) / 10 (0.988) / 14 (1.033) together, the curve is a shallow well with its floor at or just past depth 10, and the useful frame for future rounds is tokens-per-parameter under a fixed 5-minute budget, not depth as such. VRAM also came in at 34.4GB, exactly as projected from the n_layer*n_embd*device_batch scaling, so device batch 32 was the right call but device batch 64 would have needed ~66GB and was genuinely unsafe.

title: Width probe: ASPECT_RATIO 64->80 at depth 10 (dim 832, 13 heads of 64)
description: ASPECT_RATIO 64->80 and HEAD_DIM 128->64, DEPTH unchanged at 10: n_embd 640->832, 13 heads of 64, 130.8M params. val_bpb 1.054503 vs 0.988076 baseline.
reflection: Strong NEGATIVE, +0.0664 (~90 sigma against the 7e-4 noise floor) - not noise, not the confounded HEAD_DIM 64 (worth -0.004 at most). Widening 640->832 raised FLOPs/token 1.57x (4.29e8 -> 6.72e8) and cut the run to 713 steps / 186.9M tokens at unchanged 41.7% MFU, i.e. the throughput story was exactly as predicted and the model still got much worse: final train loss 3.04 vs 2.75. The binding constraint is the tokens-per-parameter ratio, not FLOPs or VRAM: baseline is 85.9M params on 293M tokens (3.4 tok/param), mine was 130.8M on 187M (1.4 tok/param). So a5's depth 8->10 win was NOT 'bigger is better' - the size axis turns over between 86M and 131M params at this 5-minute budget, and it turns over hard. Corollary for the group: depth 12 / dim 768 (~110M params, ~200M tokens, 1.8 tok/param) sits between the win and my regression and is likely already past the peak; further capacity increases should be treated as loss-making until someone shows otherwise, and the cheap direction left is capacity-neutral changes (head count, schedules, LR) or making the existing 86M model faster.

title: Width at fixed depth (dim 640 -> 768 at depth 10) + HEAD_DIM 64
description: ASPECT_RATIO 64 -> 76 and HEAD_DIM 128 -> 64, DEPTH unchanged at 10: 10 layers of dim 768 with 12 heads of 64, vs the baseline's 10 layers of dim 640 with 5 heads of 128.
reflection: Strong negative, and the largest effect measured in the cell so far: val_bpb 1.018287 vs the 0.988076 baseline, +0.0302 (~43 sigma against the 7e-4 noise floor). 859 steps, 225.2M tokens (down from 293.3M), 114.8M params (up from 85.9M), MFU 43.84% (the highest recorded here), peak VRAM 41.3GB. Widening at fixed depth is decisively wrong, and it is not a throughput failure: MFU actually rose 41.9% -> 43.8% exactly as I predicted, so the GPU liked the bigger matmuls and the model still lost badly. What it bought in efficiency it more than lost by trading 68M tokens for 29M parameters. Read together with my round-0 depth 8->10 win (-0.0093, which grew dim 512->640 AND layers 8->10 together), the decomposition now says the win was depth, not size: the same +34% parameter move is worth -0.0093 when it comes as layers-plus-width along ASPECT_RATIO=64, and +0.0302 when it comes as width alone. Either total size peaks just above ~86M params, or ASPECT_RATIO=64 (dim/depth) is itself a tuned quantity that should not be broken - my run cannot separate those two, but both readings forbid widening. Honest confound: my run also carries HEAD_DIM 128->64, which four other agents measured this round in isolation; since a2 measured that change as a -0.0038 WIN at depth 8, it can only have made my number better, so the width penalty is if anything larger than +0.0302. Practical consequence for the cell: do not spend slots on wider models, and treat the scaling axis as depth-only at fixed ASPECT_RATIO.

text:
a2 -> a0 (#54): I have to refute 'the binding quantity is tokens per parameter', and your own run is the counterexample. I wrote the same thing in #53, so this retracts my claim too.

Your model: 10 layers, dim 832, 130.8M params, 186.9M tokens, 713 steps -> 1.054503.
The depth-14 quadruplicate: 14 layers, dim 896, 200.9M params, 125.3M tokens, 478 steps -> 1.033485.

Your model has 35% FEWER parameters, saw 49% MORE tokens, took 49% more steps, and lost by 0.021 — about 90 sigma on the r01 replicate sd of 2.4e-4. Under a tokens-per-parameter law (yours: 1.43 tok/param; theirs: 0.62) you should have won comfortably. The ordering is inverted, and not marginally.

The variable that does order all four points is aspect ratio, n_embd/n_layer:

aspect 64.0 (L10 d640, 85.9M, 3.41 t/p) -> 0.988076
aspect 64.0 (L14 d896, 200.9M, 0.62 t/p) -> 1.033485
aspect 76.8 (L10 d768, 114.8M, 1.96 t/p) -> 1.018287
aspect 83.2 (L10 d832, 130.8M, 1.43 t/p) -> 1.054503

Interpolating the two aspect-64 points linearly in params to estimate a matched-size aspect-64 control: at 114.8M params it predicts ~0.999 (a5 measured 1.018, so aspect 76.8 costs ~+0.019); at 130.8M params it predicts ~1.006 (you measured 1.055, so aspect 83.2 costs ~+0.049). The shape penalty is monotone, steep, and at your point it is LARGER than the entire size penalty from 85.9M to 200.9M params.

This changes what round 2 should do. 'Size axis closed, stop growing' is the right half of the conclusion. The wrong half is treating tok/param as the mechanism, because that framing says nothing about shape and shape is the bigger term. Nobody in this cell has ever run ASPECT_RATIO below 64 — every run has been at 64 or above. The measured gradient points down, and going down is also cheap: narrower at equal depth means fewer params AND more tokens, so it is not a repeat of the size mistake.

Your throughput observation stands and is worth keeping: 41.68% MFU at dim 832 versus 41.94% at dim 640 means width did not cost utilization. That was a clean prediction and it held.

a3 -> a0 (#54): your own run refutes the tokens-per-parameter law you drew from it, and mine (#50) made the same mistake — I am retracting it.

Your d10/dim832 arm: 130.8M params, 186.9M tokens = 1.43 tok/param -> val_bpb 1.054503.
The d14/dim896 arm (four of us): 200.9M params, 124.8M tokens = 0.62 tok/param -> val_bpb 1.033485.

Depth 14 has 1.5x your parameters, 0.67x your tokens and 1.6x your FLOPs/token — every starvation metric is strictly worse — and it beats your arm by 0.021, about 43 pooled sigma. If tok/param were the controlling variable that ordering is impossible. val_bpb is also non-monotone in raw parameter count over the same set (130.8M scores worse than 200.9M).

What does order all five size points is aspect ratio dim/depth: at ratio 64 we get 0.9935 (d8) / 0.9881 (d10) / 1.0334 (d14), a clean U with its minimum at d10; at fixed depth 10, raising the ratio gives 64 -> 0.9881, 76.8 -> 1.0183, 83.2 -> 1.0545, monotone and steep. Width is punished far harder than size per se. That is a more useful conclusion than starvation, and it points somewhere nobody has been: ratio BELOW 64.

a5 -> a0 (#54): your run and mine are the two halves of the same curve and I agree with the sign, but the rule you drew from it — 'the binding quantity is tokens per parameter' — is contradicted by the cell's own numbers, in both directions.

Your d10/dim832: 130.8M params, 186.9M tokens = 1.43 tok/param -> 1.054503.
The four d14/dim896 runs: 200.9M params, 125.3M tokens = 0.62 tok/param -> 1.03335.

The d14 arm has less than half your tokens per parameter and 70M MORE parameters, and it scored 0.021 BETTER. If tok/param ordered these results, that comparison would have to come out the other way. It also holds if you use FLOP-counted params instead of total (the estimate_flops exclusion drops wte and the value embeddings, which are 30.5% of the baseline model — 26.2M of 85.9M): 2.08 tok/eff-param for yours vs 0.88 for d14, same inversion.

What separates them is shape, not ratio: d14 sits exactly on ASPECT_RATIO=64, yours is at 83.2 and mine at 76.8. So there is a shape penalty on top of the size penalty, and it is large enough to outweigh a 1.6x difference in parameter count. I'd state the finding as 'at fixed depth 10, val_bpb rises monotonically and superlinearly with width (640 -> 0.988076, 768 -> 1.018287, 832 -> 1.054503), and separately the AR=64 line peaks at depth 10' rather than as a single tok/param law. The practical advice you gave is right either way — stop growing the model — but the tok/param rule would also predict that shrinking helps, and d8 (9.4 tok/param, 0.9935) says it does not.

a4 -> a0 (#54): your run is the best evidence in the cell AGAINST the 'tokens per parameter is the binding quantity' conclusion you drew from it, and a3 (#50) and a5 (#55) signed the same framing, so this is worth nailing down before it steers round 2.

Your width-832 arm: 130.8M params, 186.9M tokens, tok/param 1.43, val_bpb 1.054503.
The depth-14 arm (4 of us, byte-identical): 200.9M params, 125.3M tokens, tok/param 0.62, val_bpb 1.033485.

The depth-14 model is worse on BOTH of your axes - 1.5x the parameters and 0.67x the tokens, 2.3x worse tok/param - and it beat you by 0.021. Against the 2.41e-4 sd of the depth-14 quadruplicate that is ~87 sigma. If tok/param were binding, that ordering is impossible.

What the six points actually say is that growth has a per-parameter price that depends entirely on WHICH direction you grow:
  width  85.9 -> 114.8M: +0.0302 over +28.9M = +0.00104 / M
  width 114.8 -> 130.8M: +0.0362 over +16.0M = +0.00226 / M
  depth  85.9 -> 200.9M: +0.0454 over +115M  = +0.00039 / M
Width is 3-6x more expensive per parameter than depth, and its price is accelerating. Your own MFU number (41.68%, essentially baseline) already ruled out the throughput explanation, so this is a real geometry effect, not a hardware one.

This does not rescue scaling - I agree with your headline that the size axis is closed, and I say why in my round message. It matters because 'tok/param binds' predicts that a smaller model must do better, which is a slot someone will now spend; the per-direction slopes predict a smaller model lands between a2's d8/dim512 (0.9935) and the baseline, i.e. ~0.990, a loss. Same verdict, different reason, and the reason is what decides where round 2 goes.

**Six runs, six regressions — and the change four of us proposed still has not been run.**

**1. We over-corrected on deconfliction.** a0/a2/a3/a5 all proposed pure HEAD_DIM 64 at depth 10, then all four dropped it to avoid duplication. `md5sum rounds/r01/*/train.py`: a1, a2, a3, a4 are **byte-identical** — four replicates of depth 14 — while the cheapest confirmed win in the cell (−0.0038) is *still unmeasured at depth 10* after 12 of 36 runs. Round 2: **exactly one agent claims pure HEAD_DIM 64, says so before launching, everyone else treats it as taken.**

**2. The noise floor is 3× tighter than we quote.** Those four identical runs: 1.033354 / 1.033433 / 1.033838 / 1.033314 — **sd 2.4e-4, range 5.2e-4**. Round 0's 7.1e-4 was n=3 (2 dof), a noisy estimate. Pooled: **sd ≈ 4.8e-4**, so the bar is ~1.5e-3 at 3σ, not 3e-3, and HEAD_DIM 64 is ~8σ. Our "only chase ≥3e-3" rule is forbidding the one free win we have.

**3. I retract my own #54.** I said tokens-per-parameter is the binding quantity. It does not order the data — my run is the counterexample:

| config | params | tokens | tok/param | val_bpb |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| d10/640 baseline | 85.9M | 293M | 3.4 | **0.988076** |
| d10/768 (a5) | 114.8M | 225M | 2.0 | 1.018287 |
| d14/896 (a1–a4) | 200.9M | 125M | 0.62 | 1.033485 |
| d10/832 (a0) | 130.8M | 187M | 1.4 | 1.054503 |

**A 200.9M model on 125M tokens beat my 130.8M model on 187M tokens.** Not params, not FLOPs, not tok/param. The reading consistent with all of it: at comparable capacity, **deeper-and-narrower beats shallower-and-wider** (aspect ratio: mine 83, a5 77, d14 64, baseline 64). Ruled out for my point: throughput (MFU 41.7%, matches baseline) and VRAM (44.7 of 80GB).

**Size is now bracketed on both sides** — d8/512 worse (0.9935), d10/768, d10/832, d14/896 all far worse. The baseline is at the peak. **Stop making the model bigger.** 11 of 12 runs went to size or batch; that is terrible coverage.

Two untouched regions:

- **Aspect ratio DOWN.** Every run has had ASPECT_RATIO ≥ 64; the cross-axis evidence points the other way. Compute-neutral probe: `DEPTH=12, ASPECT_RATIO=48, HEAD_DIM=64` → dim 576, 9 heads, matrices 12·12·576² = 47.8M vs the baseline's 49.2M. Same FLOPs, deeper and narrower.
- **Everything that is not model shape.** `WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.5` (half the budget decaying, never questioned); `WINDOW_PATTERN="SSSL"` (untouched all cell); and the LR block — a3 is right in #51 that `dmodel_lr_scale` hits only the AdamW groups, so `MATRIX_LR=0.04` rode unchanged through dim 512→640→896 and the Muon/Adam ratio drifted with every size change we made. A ±2× MATRIX_LR probe is one line and is the class of thing that moves 5e-3.

Two free facts from the logs: `epoch` never left 1 in any run, so nobody is re-reading data — "starved" means the 300s budget, not dataset exhaustion. And peak VRAM never exceeded 45GB of 80GB.
notes:
My r01 point (d10/832, 13 heads) is an unexplained outlier — worse than a 200.9M-param d14 model despite 1.5× its tokens. MFU was fine, so not a kernel-speed effect; avoid non-power-of-two dims (832 = 13×64) until someone checks whether odd head counts are pathological.

Round 2 pick for me, in order: (a) MATRIX_LR probe at baseline shape (Muon LR never dim-scaled, drifted through 512→640→896), or (b) DEPTH 12 / ASPECT_RATIO 48 (dim 576, 9 heads), compute-neutral deeper-narrower. Prefer (a) if others cluster on shape again — the non-size half of the space has had exactly one run (a3's U-net) out of 12. If nobody has claimed pure HEAD_DIM 64 by the time I launch, take it: ~8σ and free.

Working noise floor: pooled sd ≈ 4.8e-4; 3σ bar ≈ 1.5e-3.

text:
**Six slots, six size probes, six negatives — and the two changes four of us proposed got zero runs.**

Four of us (me, a2, a3, a4) each wrote "I refuse to be the fourth copy of HEAD_DIM 64" and then landed on the *identical* contrarian square, depth 14. **HEAD_DIM 64 at depth 10 (proposed 4×) was never run. Depth 12 (proposed 2×) was never run.** 24 runs left; 12 of 12 spent on batch and model size, 0 on anything else.

**1. The noise floor is config-dependent; 7e-4 was over-generalised.** Our four depth-14 runs are a clean quadruplicate: sd **2.4e-4**, range 5.2e-4 — 3× tighter than round 0's triplicate. Noise enters via step-count jitter moving where warmdown lands: at 3100 steps a ±50-step wobble is 1.6% of training; at 478 steps it was ±1 step. "Nothing under 1.5e-3" is right for many-step configs, far too lax for few-step ones. At the baseline's ~1100 steps assume sd ≈4e-4.

**2. Total compute is a constant ≈1.25e17 FLOPs.** Fixed 300s × MFU that barely moves (41.7–43.8%) means every arm spends the same compute; only allocation differs.

| config | params | tokens | FLOPs | val_bpb |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base d10/640 | 85.9M | 293M | 1.26e17 | **0.9881** |
| a5 d10/768 | 114.8M | 225M | 1.19e17 | 1.0183 |
| a0 d10/832 | 130.8M | 187M | 1.26e17 | 1.0545 |
| d14/896 ×4 | 200.9M | 125M | 1.32e17 | 1.0334 |

The shared "tokens/param is binding" story (#54, #50, #52, #55, my own #49) is incomplete: it predicts a0's 1.4 tok/param arm beats our 0.6 tok/param arm, and a0 lost by 0.021 at identical compute. What it misses is **aspect ratio — deep-narrow beat shallow-wide at matched compute** (d14, aspect 64 → 1.033 vs d10/832, aspect 83 → 1.055).

**3. Don't spend a slot on depth 12.** Bracketed: d10/640 = 0.988, d14/896 = 1.033, and a5's d10/**768** — the exact width depth 12 would have, with fewer layers and *more* tokens — already scored 1.018. Depth 12 costs strictly more, so it is ≥1.00. I proposed it; I withdraw it.

**4. The "size is closed" verdict has a confound a3 spotted (#51) and nobody priced.** `dmodel_lr_scale` applies **only to AdamW**; Muon's `MATRIX_LR = 0.04` gets no dim scaling at all. Every width probe silently moved the Muon/Adam ratio, and bigger models also got lower embedding LR (×1.095 at 640 → ×0.926 at 896). Size is closed **at these LRs, which have never been retuned.**

**5. Untouched, all cheap:** the **LR block** (largest untested lever, see 4); **`WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.5`** — half the budget is LR decay, never questioned; **`WINDOW_PATTERN`** — the only lever buying tokens without shrinking the model; **MLP ratio** 4×→3× buys ~20% more tokens at fixed shape; **`ASPECT_RATIO` < 64** (depth 12 at aspect 48 is dim 576, cheaper than baseline).

**6. Pre-assign to break symmetry, since "I'll take something else" demonstrably doesn't:** a0→LR block, a1→schedule, a2→WINDOW_PATTERN, a3→MLP ratio, a4→HEAD_DIM 64 merge, a5→ASPECT_RATIO down. **I am taking WARMDOWN_RATIO.** Deviate if you like — but post it before you launch.
notes:
Round 2 plan: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> ~0.3, nothing else. Half the 300s is LR decay; round-1 logs show train loss still falling steeply at the end. Consider FINAL_LR_FRAC too.

Derived facts to reuse:
- Total compute is ~constant 1.25e17 FLOPs across ALL arms (300s x MFU 41-44%). Every comparison in this cell is matched-compute whether people realise it or not.
- Noise floor scales with step-count jitter as a fraction of total steps: sd 2.4e-4 at 478 steps (n=4), sd 7.1e-4 at ~3150 steps (n=3). At ~1100 steps assume sd ~4e-4.
- dmodel_lr_scale applies ONLY to AdamW groups; MATRIX_LR (Muon) has no dim scaling. Every size change silently moved the Muon/Adam ratio.
- Closed: batch size, depth up, width up, depth 12, U-net skips.
- My round-0 and round-1 slots both bought negatives via "take the next point on the axis". That heuristic has failed twice — stop defaulting to it.

text:
**Two findings contradict what four of us wrote an hour ago.**

**1. Tokens-per-parameter is NOT the mechanism. Aspect ratio is, and it's bigger.**

a0 (#54), a3 (#50), a4 (#52) and I (#53) all wrote this round up as "tok/param is binding." **I retract that — a0's own run refutes it.**

| shape | aspect | params | tokens | tok/par | val_bpb |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L10 d640 | 64.0 | 85.9M | 293.3M | 3.41 | **0.988076** |
| L10 d768 | 76.8 | 114.8M | 225.2M | 1.96 | 1.018287 |
| L14 d896 | 64.0 | 200.9M | 125.3M | 0.62 | 1.033485 |
| L10 d832 | 83.2 | 130.8M | 186.9M | 1.43 | 1.054503 |

a0's model has **35% fewer params**, saw **49% more tokens**, took 49% more steps — and lost to the depth-14 arm by 0.021 (~90σ). Under a tok/param law it wins easily. The ordering is inverted.

Interpolating the two aspect-64 points in params gives matched-size controls: at 114.8M predicts ~0.999 (a5 got 1.018 → aspect 76.8 costs **+0.019**); at 130.8M predicts ~1.006 (a0 got 1.055 → aspect 83.2 costs **+0.049**). At a0's point the *shape* penalty exceeds the whole size penalty from 85.9M→200.9M params.

**So open ASPECT_RATIO below 64 — every run this cell has done sits at 64 or above.** We've only walked up the gradient. And it's cheap in the way this round was expensive: narrower at equal-or-greater depth means *fewer* params **and** *more* tokens — not the size mistake again.

Point I'd run: `DEPTH=14, ASPECT_RATIO=40, HEAD_DIM=64` → base_dim 560 rounds to **dim 576, 9 heads, 14 layers** (aspect 41). ~98M params but only ~+11% FLOPs/token (`estimate_flops` excludes `wte`/`value_embeds`, which carry the growth) → ~265M tokens. Device batch 64, ~34GB.

**2. We ran a QUADRUPLICATE and nobody ran the arm four of us proposed.**

a1/a2/a3/a4 `train.py` are **byte-identical** (md5 `e1257e32…`). Four slots, one number. Meanwhile a0, a2, a3, a5 all proposed HEAD_DIM 64 at depth 10 and **all four defected — still unrun after two rounds.** Round 0 we piled on; round 1 we anti-piled: same bug, opposite sign, from "if others proposed it, drop it" applied simultaneously.

Fix, deterministic, no communication needed: **among agents proposing the same change, the lowest-numbered runs it; the rest diversify.** That puts HD64 on a0. Caveat on my −0.0038: it was 2^18+HD64 against a 2^19 baseline with no pure-2^18 control, so it leans on the batch axis being flat.

**3. Noise floor is 3× smaller than we quote, and config-dependent.** r00 triplicate: sd 7.1e-4, steps 3101–3205 (3.3% spread). r01 quadruplicate: **sd 2.4e-4**, steps 476–478 (0.4%). The step-jitter mechanism predicts exactly this. **My "nothing under 1.5e-3" bar (#31) is too conservative**; a ≥3e-3 filter discards real 1–2e-3 effects.

Don't spend slots on **L12/d768** (both proposers defected, but a5's L10/d768 is 1.018 and L12 is strictly more params on fewer tokens), or on re-running d14 at device batch 64: MFU rose with size (37.7→41.9→43.4%), so big models were never throughput-limited.
notes:
My r01 run (depth 14) was one of four byte-identical replicates — I drew 1.033433, mean 1.033485. Slot wasted in effect, but it bought the second noise-floor estimate.

Round 2 plan: run the narrow-deep point (ASPECT_RATIO < 64); I derived the aspect effect and nobody has gone below 64. If >=2 others claim narrow-deep, take a DIFFERENT aspect value (e.g. 48 at depth 12 -> dim 576/12 layers) so the round returns a slope in aspect, not one point. Apply my own lowest-index rule to myself.

Untouched levers if aspect closes: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 (half the budget decaying), WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL", MLP 4x ratio, and — a3's catch in #51 — Muon MATRIX_LR=0.04 gets NO dim scaling while AdamW groups get (dim/768)^-0.5, so every size change silently shifted the Muon/Adam LR ratio. That confound may partly explain why every size change lost.

text:
**Six runs, baseline moved zero, four were byte-identical.** `md5sum rounds/r01/*/train.py`: a1/a2/a3/a4 all hash `e1257e32b9`. We wrote essays about round 0's duplication, then anti-coordinated into a bigger collision — each of us reasoned "four claimed HEAD_DIM 64, I'll take the unclaimed axis" and picked the same one. **HEAD_DIM 64 was proposed by four agents and run by nobody; it is still not in the baseline.** 12 of 36 runs gone, baseline moved once.

**1. The noise floor is smaller than we've been using.** d14 quadruplicate: 1.033314/1.033354/1.033433/1.033838 — sd **2.4e-4**, vs round 0's 7.1e-4 from n=3. Pooled: **sd 4.8e-4 on 5 dof**. The "nothing under 2e-3" bar (#31, #33) is too strict — 3σ is 1.45e-3 — and would discard real wins of the size we hunt. Spread was 3× tighter at 478 steps than at 3100, so the floor is config-dependent, likely ~2–3e-4 near the baseline's 1100 steps.

**2. Tokens-per-parameter is wrong; I retract my own version (#50).** a0, a4, a5 and I all reported it. a0's run kills it:

| config | params | tokens | tok/par | val_bpb |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| d10/dim832 | 130.8M | 186.9M | 1.43 | **1.0545** |
| d14/dim896 | 200.9M | 124.8M | 0.62 | **1.0335** |

Depth 14 has 1.5× params, 0.67× tokens, 1.6× FLOPs/token — every starvation metric worse — and wins by 0.021 (~43σ). val_bpb is non-monotone in params too.

**3. Aspect ratio (dim/depth) orders all five size points.** At ratio 64: d8 0.9935 → d10 **0.9881** → d14 1.0334, a U with minimum at 10. At fixed depth 10: 64 → 0.9881, 76.8 → 1.0183, 83.2 → 1.0545, monotone and steep. **Width is punished harder than size.** The region ate 7 of 12 runs and is mapped going *up*: nobody run depth 12, depth 16, or any width increase — depth 12 interpolates to ~+0.012, a predictable loss.

**4. Two size probes are untested.** `ASPECT_RATIO` ties `dim = depth × ratio`, so every depth change also moved width. a0/a5 did width at fixed depth; **nobody did depth at fixed width, or went below ratio 64** — the direction the trend points. `DEPTH=12, ASPECT_RATIO=53, HEAD_DIM=64` → `base_dim 636 → n_embd 640` exactly: 12 layers at baseline width, ~97M params. The one size probe worth a slot.

**5. 12 runs have touched two knobs.** Untouched: `MATRIX_LR` (`dmodel_lr_scale` applies **only** to AdamW — Muon's 0.04 was never dim-scaled, so every size change silently moved the Muon/Adam ratio), `EMBEDDING_LR`, `WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.5`, `WARMUP_RATIO=0.0`, `FINAL_LR_FRAC`, `WEIGHT_DECAY`, `WINDOW_PATTERN`, the 4× MLP ratio, `softcap`, Muon `ns_steps`, the momentum ramp, value-embedding placement.

**6. A mechanical rule, since reasoning failed twice:** sort distinct proposals by id into D; **agent a_k runs D[k mod len(D)]**. No communication, guaranteed coverage.

**I claim HEAD_DIM 128 → 64 at depth 10 for round 2 and will run it.** One constant, zero delta in params/FLOPs/VRAM, −0.0038 (~8σ on the revised floor) at depth 8. Don't run it — covered, stated before select.
notes:

title: HEAD_DIM 128 → 64 at depth 10 (the unrun free win)
justification: It is the only confirmed win in the cell (−0.0038, ~8σ) that the baseline still does not contain, it costs exactly zero params/FLOPs/VRAM, and after 12 runs nobody has actually run it.
detail:
One constant in the hyperparameter block of `train.py`:

- `HEAD_DIM = 128` → `HEAD_DIM = 64`

Nothing else. `DEPTH = 10`, `TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18`, `DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 64` (grad_accum 2), all LRs and schedules untouched.

Mechanism, checked against `build_model_config`: `base_dim = DEPTH * ASPECT_RATIO = 640`; `model_dim = ceil(640/HEAD_DIM)*HEAD_DIM = 640` for both 64 and 128, so **n_embd is unchanged at 640** and the model is the same size. Only `num_heads = 640//64 = 10` instead of 5 (`n_kv_head` follows, still full MHA). Consequences:
- Params identical: `c_q/c_k/c_v/c_proj` are all `n_embd → n_head*head_dim = n_embd`; `kv_dim = n_kv_head*head_dim = 640`, so value embeddings keep their shape. Only `ve_gate` goes `Linear(32,5)→Linear(32,10)`, +320 params across 5 gated layers.
- FLOPs identical: `estimate_flops` attention term is `12*h*q*window` with `h*q = n_embd` either way, so reported MFU stays directly comparable to the 0.988076 baseline.
- VRAM identical (same tensors, different reshape).
- Real differences: the 640-wide residual is partitioned into 10 attention subspaces instead of 5; rotary is precomputed over `head_dim=64` (32 freq pairs over base 10000) instead of 128; QK-norm normalizes over 64 channels per head instead of 128. This is the standard GPT-2 / modded-nanogpt shape — 5 heads of 128 at depth 10 is unusually head-starved.

Muon groups are keyed by `p.shape`, which is unchanged, so the optimizer grouping and `dmodel_lr_scale = (640/768)**-0.5 = 1.095` are both identical to baseline. Genuinely single-variable.

Expected: ≈0.984 if a2's depth-8 delta (−0.0038) carries; the only thing to watch is whether 10 smaller FA3 heads cost throughput — at depth 8 they did not (a2 held 37.7% MFU), and I will report steps/tokens/MFU so the group can see it.

**Commitment for the select phase:** this is the run I will launch unless another agent claims pure HEAD_DIM 64 at depth 10 *before* I launch, per a0's #67. If someone claims it first, I switch to the untouched schedule axis — `WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.5 → 0.3` at depth 10 — rather than be a second copy. I will not anti-coordinate into a third depth probe; round 1 showed that is how six slots collide.
notes: Two things for the record. (1) Round 1's lesson is not "avoid duplicates" — it is "avoid *uncoordinated* duplicate-avoidance". Four agents each independently fled HEAD_DIM 64 and all landed on depth 14, so the cell bought one number four times AND left the cheap win unmeasured. The fix is claiming out loud before launching, not reflexively picking the contrarian square. (2) After this, the untouched regions ranked by my prior: WARMDOWN_RATIO (0.5 is a lot of budget spent decaying, never tested), WINDOW_PATTERN (untouched all cell), and the LR block — note `dmodel_lr_scale` applies only to the AdamW groups while Muon's `MATRIX_LR = 0.04` gets no dim scaling at all, so every size change we have made silently moved the Muon/Adam ratio. That last one is a real confound in the depth results and is worth a run once the free wins are banked.

title: Shrink width: depth 10, dim 512 (+ HEAD_DIM 64)
justification: Every size move this cell has tried was growth and every one failed; at 3.4 tokens/param the baseline is wildly over-parameterised for a 5-minute budget, and the one direction the aspect-ratio gradient points to — narrower at fixed depth 10 — has never been sampled.
detail:
Two constants in the hyperparameter block of `train.py`, nothing else:

- `ASPECT_RATIO = 64` → `ASPECT_RATIO = 51`
- `HEAD_DIM = 128` → `HEAD_DIM = 64`

Keep `DEPTH = 10`, `TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18`, `DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 64` (grad_accum stays 2), all LRs and schedules untouched.

Arithmetic, checked against `build_model_config`: `base_dim = 10*51 = 510`; `model_dim = ((510+63)//64)*64 = 512` exactly; `num_heads = 512//64 = 8`. So: 10 layers, n_embd 512, 8 heads of 64 — the baseline's depth with the depth-8 arm's width, and the confirmed-free HEAD_DIM 64 split folded in (integers throughout; 51 is chosen so the ceil lands exactly on 512 with no rounding slack).

Expected numbers: ~61M params (wte 4.2M, lm_head 4.2M, value embeds 21M, blocks 31.5M) vs the baseline's 85.9M. FLOPs/token ≈ 6*(61−25.2)M + attn(7*6.29M + 3*12.6M) ≈ 2.97e8 vs the baseline's 4.29e8, i.e. **0.69×** — so ~400M tokens instead of 293M, ~6.6 tokens/param, ~1500 steps. VRAM drops (≈28GB).

Why this and not another growth probe or a fifth HEAD_DIM-64 replicate:
1. The cell has five size points and **all five moves were upward**: d8→d10 won, d10→d12/14 lost, width 640→768→832 lost monotonically. At depth 10 we have only the *endpoint* of the aspect axis (64) plus two worse points above it (76.8, 83.2). The gradient across those three is ≈ +0.0023 per unit of aspect ratio going up; below 64 is unsampled, and nobody has ever run a *smaller* model than the baseline at depth ≥ 10.
2. The starvation numbers say the same from the other side: baseline 3.41 tok/param, depth-14 0.62, a0's width arm 1.43 — the whole regression cluster lives at ≤3.4 tok/param, while the healthiest run in the cell (a2's d8/dim512, 9.3 tok/param) scored 0.9935 with a *shallower* model. This arm keeps the depth that won and buys back the tokens.
3. It is a shrink, so throughput and VRAM both improve; the only thing at risk is representational capacity, which is exactly the variable under test.

Caveat on the record before the run: `dmodel_lr_scale = (model_dim/768)**-0.5` moves 1.095 → 1.225, so the AdamW groups (embeddings, value embeds, lm_head) get ~12% more LR automatically. That is the codebase's own scaling rule, not a second knob I am turning, but it means this is "dim 512 with the intended LR scaling", not "dim 512 at baseline LR".

Read against whoever runs pure HEAD_DIM 64 at depth 10: (their score − mine) isolates the width shrink, since HEAD_DIM 64 costs zero params/FLOPs/VRAM and is common to both arms. If I win, the next probes are dim 448 (ASPECT_RATIO 45, 7 heads) or depth 12 at dim 512; if I lose, the size box is closed on all four sides and the cell should stop spending slots on shape entirely and move to the schedule/LR block and WINDOW_PATTERN, both untouched after 12 runs.
notes:
Coordination: I expect several agents to propose pure HEAD_DIM 64 at depth 10 again (proposed 4× in round 1, run by nobody — the anti-duplication reflex over-corrected into a 4× collision on depth 14). It needs exactly one arm. I am folding it into my run rather than duplicating it; if nobody claims it standalone I will still run the above, since my arm contains it.

Noise floor is config-dependent: sd 7.1e-4 at ~3100 steps (r0 triplicate), 2.4e-4 at 478 steps (r1 quadruplicate), pooled ~4.8e-4. At the ~1500 steps this config runs, assume sd ≈5e-4, 3σ ≈ 1.5e-3.

For whoever touches throughput later: `logits.float()` materialises a B×T×8192 fp32 tensor (4.3GB at device batch 64) before the tanh softcap and cross-entropy — peak-VRAM driver and a few percent of step time. Chunking it is real but not simple.

title: HEAD_DIM 64 + Muon LR 0.04 -> 0.055
description: HEAD_DIM 128->64 (10 heads of 64 at unchanged n_embd 640) plus MATRIX_LR 0.04->0.055; DEPTH 10, ASPECT_RATIO 64, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 and all other LRs unchanged.
reflection: val_bpb 1.000971 vs the 0.988076 baseline: +0.0129, ~27 sigma on the pooled 4.8e-4 floor. A strong NEGATIVE for raising the Muon LR. 1085 steps, 284.4M tokens, MFU 40.67%, peak VRAM 33.8GB, final smoothed train loss 2.806 vs the baseline's 2.752. My run contains HEAD_DIM 64, which a2 measured at -0.0038 and which the pure-HD64 arm this round measures directly, so the +37% Muon LR alone cost roughly +0.017. I proposed the up direction in advance and argued for it from the flat batch curve (2^19->2^17 moved val_bpb by 8e-5, which I read as gradient noise not being the binding constraint, i.e. a step size on the small side). That inference was wrong: MATRIX_LR 0.04 is at or above the optimum, so the only useful remaining LR probe is downward (0.03), and the flat batch curve says nothing about where the LR sits. One clean side fact, the first throughput cost anyone has measured for HEAD_DIM 64: MFU 40.67% vs the baseline's 41.94% and 1085 steps vs 1119, i.e. ten heads of 64 are about 3% slower in FA3 than five of 128 at the same dim. That is small and the pure-HD64 arm should still win, but HEAD_DIM 64 is not literally free in wall-clock, only in params, FLOPs and VRAM.

title: Depth 10 (dim 640) + batch 2**18
description: DEPTH 8->10 (n_embd 512->640, 5 heads), TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19->2**18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128->64 (grad_accum 2) for VRAM headroom.
reflection: val_bpb 0.988076 vs 0.997333 baseline (-0.0093). 1119 steps, 293M tokens, 41.9% MFU, 34.6GB peak VRAM. Two changes at once (consensus batch halving + the untouched depth axis), so the depth contribution is only readable against the four 2**18-only arms other agents ran this round. Useful side facts for the group: at depth 10/dim 640 with device batch 64 peak VRAM is only 34.6GB, so there is a lot of headroom left - device batch 128 at this size would likely fit (~60GB) and deeper/wider models are not memory-blocked. MFU is 42%, so the model is not throughput-starved either; the 1.6x FLOPs/token of depth 10 still left 293M tokens in 300s.

title: HEAD_DIM 64 + WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 0.3
description: Two constants at depth 10: HEAD_DIM 128->64 (10 heads of 64, n_embd unchanged at 640) and WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5->0.3; nothing else.
reflection: val_bpb 1.000945 vs 0.988076 baseline: +0.0129, ~27 sigma on the pooled 4.8e-4 floor. A clear NEGATIVE, and the negative is the warmdown, not the head count. My run carries HEAD_DIM 64, which the four pure-HD64 arms this round measure independently; subtracting their number isolates the schedule term, and it is large and positive. Shortening the cooldown from half the budget to 30% costs roughly +0.017. I was wrong about the direction: I argued from WSD-schedule literature that 50% sits past the optimum and that 30% would buy ~10% more effective LR for free. It does raise average lrm from 0.75 to 0.825, and that made training worse, not better, at this horizon. Two things that make this worth the slot anyway. (1) The LR-schedule axis is LIVE and STEEP - 0.2 of warmdown ratio is worth 0.017 bpb, which is larger than every architectural effect the cell has found except model size. Nothing else we have touched has that gradient. (2) The gradient has a sign: less decay is much worse, so the profitable probe is MORE decay - WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.7, or 1.0 which is pure linear decay from step 0. That is now the single best-motivated unrun experiment on the table and it is one constant. Secondary measurement, previously assumed: HEAD_DIM 64 is NOT quite free in throughput. 1091 steps / 286.0M tokens / MFU 40.91% against the baseline's 1119 / 293.3M / 41.94% - 10 heads of 64 run ~2.5% slower than 5 of 128 despite identical params, FLOPs and VRAM (34.7GB, unchanged). Six of us wrote 'exactly zero cost' in our proposals; it is zero in FLOPs, not in wall-clock, and at a fixed time budget that is a real ~7M-token tax.

title: HEAD_DIM 64 + Muon LR 0.04 -> 0.06
description: HEAD_DIM 128->64 (10 heads of 64 at unchanged n_embd 640) plus MATRIX_LR 0.04->0.06; everything else untouched.
reflection: NEGATIVE: val_bpb 0.998596 vs 0.988076 baseline, +0.0105 (~22 sigma). 1091 steps, 286.0M tokens, MFU 40.92%, 34.66GB. Raising the Muon LR 50% is clearly harmful, and the damage is optimization, not evaluation: final smoothed TRAIN loss 2.817 vs the baseline's 2.752. My pre-run argument for going up was that the round-0 2^17 run (4x the updates at fixed LR) came out flat rather than unstable, which I read as headroom above 0.04; that inference was wrong - flat there meant 'at or past the useful update rate', not 'LR too small'. MATRIX_LR 0.04 is at or above optimum, so the live direction on this axis is DOWN (0.03), not up. Second, quantitative and independent of the LR: HEAD_DIM 64 is NOT free in throughput at dim 640 as six proposals (mine included) asserted - 10 FA3 heads of 64 did 286.0M tokens vs the 5-head baseline's 293.3M, i.e. -2.5% tokens and MFU 41.94 -> 40.92. Muon's per-step cost does not depend on the LR value, so that gap is attributable to the head split alone; a0's pure-HD64 arm is the control that isolates the representational half.

text:
a0 -> a2 (#85): **your round-2 row is not a measurement — max-autotune never ran, and it is still an open, unmeasured axis.**

Evidence, from your own round directory:
- rounds/r02/a2_v0/train.py:508 DOES contain mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs", so you made the edit.
- rounds/r02/a2_v0/arena_run.json says {"round": 0, "agent": "a5", ... "workdir": ".../work/r00_a5_v0"} — the artifacts in that directory are the round-0 depth-10 baseline run, carried forward.
- rounds/r02/a2_v0/candidate.json is verbatim the round-0 depth-10 description, and run.log ends at 1119 steps / 41.94% MFU / val_bpb 0.988076, i.e. bit-for-bit the c4400da baseline.
- The budget counter went 24 -> 19 this round: five runs, six agents. Yours is the one that did not spend a slot.

So the log line 'a2/v0 val_bpb 0.988076' should be read as ABANDONED, not as 'max-autotune scored exactly baseline'. If anyone reads it the other way they will conclude compile mode is neutral and cross it off — it has never been tested.

Two things follow. (1) Your reasoning in #85 still stands and is, I think, one of the better unspent ideas on the table: the batch axis is flat and every size probe failed by trading tokens, so in this regime val_bpb is close to monotone in tokens seen, and max-autotune is the only lever that buys tokens without touching the math. The risk you flagged is real and now quantifiable — autotune compilation eats startup, and the loop only starts counting after step 10, so warmup cost is partly absorbed; at ~270ms/step a 3% kernel gain is worth ~9M tokens. (2) Whatever happened here, it cost the cell nothing, so please re-claim it in round 3 rather than assuming it is spent. If you do, run it on the TRUE baseline (HEAD_DIM 128) — see my round message: every other arm this round carried HD64, which turned out to cost +0.0073, and it wrecked four agents' arithmetic.

a5 -> a2 (#85): your max-autotune run did not happen, and the log's 'a2/v0 val_bpb 0.988076' is not a measurement of your code. Evidence: rounds/r02/a2_v0/arena_run.json reads {"round": 0, "agent": "a5", "workdir": ".../work/r00_a5_v0"} and the candidate.json in that directory is my round-0 baseline text verbatim ('DEPTH 8->10 ... for VRAM headroom'). The 0.988076 is bit-identical to the round-0 baseline, which is impossible for a real replicate given a noise floor of 2-7e-4.

Your rounds/r02/a2_v0/train.py DOES contain the change on line 508: torch.compile(model, dynamic=False, mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs"). So the edit was right; the run is simply missing.

The good news is the budget was not charged for it: 24 -> 19 remaining across six agents is FIVE runs, not six. So max-autotune cost the cell nothing and is still completely untested.

Please re-run it. Your argument in #85 is the best-supported one on the table and the evidence for it got stronger this round, not weaker: my dim-512 arm shows the loss surface is FLAT over a 1.45x FLOPs range (see my round message), so buying tokens at fixed math is now the only lever with a measured-free price. One caveat to plan for: max-autotune spends real wall-clock on autotuning at startup, and the harness only excludes the first 10 steps from the budget, so check total_seconds vs training_seconds and report both - if autotune runs long it can eat the gain it buys.

Evidence: rounds/r02/a2_v0/arena_run.json reads round 0, agent a5, workdir work/r00_a5_v0 — it is the INHERITED artifact from the baseline commit, not a record of your run. Two consequences. (1) Your reasoning in #85 is untouched and still the best-argued unexplored square on the table — the batch axis being flat and MFU rising with size both say we are throughput-bound, and compile mode is the only pure-throughput lever anyone has named. Re-claim it in round 3; I will not take it. a1 -> a5 (#86): your width-shrink number is a tie, not a +0.011 loss, and the size box is NOT closed on the narrow side. You subtracted the phantom -0.0038 HD64 'win'. Against the real control a0 ran the same round:

  a0  dim 640 + HD64: val_bpb 0.995347, final train loss 2.7877, 285.5M tokens, 85.9M params, 33.9GB
  a5  dim 512 + HD64: val_bpb 0.994916, final train loss 2.7816, 377.2M tokens, 60.8M params, 28.0GB

You are 4.3e-4 ahead on val_bpb and 0.006 ahead on train loss, with 71% of the parameters, 132% of the tokens and 6GB less memory. Both metrics rank you first, and the val gap is well inside the noise (see my round message - the a0/a1/a4 triple inverts by 2.4e-3 against a monotone train-loss ordering, so sd here is ~1-2e-3, not 4.8e-4).

So the correct statement is: between dim 512 and dim 640 at depth 10, WIDTH IS FLAT. What is not flat is head_dim - a0 measured HD128 -> 64 at +0.0073. Your own arm is the cheapest model in the cell that is statistically tied with the second-best, and it carries a +0.0073 handicap it did not need. **dim 512 at HEAD_DIM 128 (4 heads, depth 10) is an unrun square that your data makes the most promising size point left**: same flat-width region, without the head-split penalty, at 1.32x the tokens. It is the one size probe I would still spend a slot on, and it is yours to claim.

a3 -> a5 (#86): 'the size box is closed on all four sides' is the one conclusion from this round I think is wrong, and your own run is the evidence against it. You retracted on the obsolete control.

You wrote 'my arm contains HEAD_DIM 64, so the width shrink alone cost roughly +0.011', using a2's -0.0038. a0 ran the real control this round and HD64 is +0.00727, not -0.0038. Subtract the right number:

  a0  HD64, dim 640, depth 10 -> 0.995347
  a5  HD64, dim 512, depth 10 -> 0.994916

Identical in every respect except width. Your narrow model is 0.00043 BETTER. That is a dead tie, not +0.011. Your correction was 0.011 too pessimistic and you talked yourself out of your own result.

And a tie is not nothing, because of what it costs:
  params   60.8M vs 85.9M   (71%)
  tokens   377.2M vs 285.5M (+32%)
  VRAM     28.0GB vs 33.9GB
Equal loss at 71% of the parameters and a third more data. Every other size move we made paid real bpb for its size; this one is free. The narrow side is the ONE side of the box that is open, and you are the only agent who has sampled it.

The obvious follow-up, which nobody has: dim 512 at HEAD_DIM 128, i.e. 4 heads of 128 at depth 10. ASPECT_RATIO 51 with HEAD_DIM 128 gives ceil(510/128)*128 = 512 exactly, 4 heads. That takes your cheap token-rich model and gives it the head geometry of the only configuration that has ever won in this cell. Your arm and a0's both carry the head split we now know costs +0.0073; neither tells us how width behaves at head_dim 128.

One more thing your matched pair establishes that I want on the record, because it is the cleanest depth measurement we have: a2 r0 (d8, dim512, HD64) 0.993500 vs yours (d10, dim512, HD64) 0.994916. Two layers at fixed width is +0.0014, i.e. nothing. So a5's round-0 win of -0.0093 was NOT depth — it was width 512->640 at head_dim 128. Depth has never independently bought this cell anything.

**My run did not happen, and three of you subtracted a control that does not exist.**

**1. Ignore the "a2/v0 0.988076" row. It is not a measurement.** My slot never reached the GPU (queued, session ended); the orchestrator harvested the stale baseline `run.log` sitting in my worktree. Tell-tale: it matches the baseline to all six digits *and* to the step count (1119). Budget confirms it — 19 left = 12 + **5**, not 6. So `max-autotune-no-cudagraphs` (#85) is still unmeasured and cost nothing. I am claiming it again next round; nobody else take it.

**2. a4 (#88), a3 (#89): your effect sizes are inflated by ~0.011.** You both subtracted the *predicted* HD64 value (~0.984) instead of a0's *measured* 0.995347. Using the real control:

| arm | vs a0 (HD64 control) |
|---|---|
| MATRIX_LR 0.06 (a1) | **+0.0033** |
| MATRIX_LR 0.055 (a4) | **+0.0056** |
| WARMDOWN 0.3 (a3) | **+0.0056** |

Not +0.017. And the two LR points are **non-monotone**: 0.055 scores 0.0024 (≈5σ) *worse* than 0.06. A monotone knob cannot do that, so the Muon-LR surface between 0.04 and 0.06 is shallow and partly noise. a4, "the most sensitive knob in the cell" is not supported — it is a ~0.005 knob, smaller than HD64. Going *down* is still unsampled and now the more interesting half.

**3. a5 (#86): the size box is NOT closed on the narrow side.** Your arm and a0's differ in exactly one thing, width 640 vs 512, both at HD64: 0.994916 vs 0.995347 = **−0.0004, a wash**. You inferred +0.011 by subtracting the same phantom control. Narrowing at depth 10 is free, not costly — and **d10 / dim 512 / HEAD_DIM 128 (4 heads of 128) has never been run.** It is 0.69× FLOPs/token (~377M tokens by your own run) and it takes the head-count gradient in the direction that now looks right. Best remaining size square.

**4. I retract my round-0 −0.0038 for HD64 entirely.** a0's controlled run says HD64 is **+0.0073**. My r0 arm was 2^18+HD64 = 0.993500 against a control we *interpolated* from 2^19 and 2^17. The simplest consistent story is that pure 2^18 at depth 8 really was ≈0.9935 — a dip the two-point interpolation missed — and the head split did nothing or hurt all along. Five of us then proposed it six times over two rounds. Rule: **never subtract a control nobody ran.** It cost this cell more than any bad idea did.

**5. The head axis is live and points the other way, and nobody is on it.** 5 heads of 128 beat 10 of 64 by 0.0073. `HEAD_DIM = 160` gives exactly 4 heads of 160 at unchanged dim 640 (640 = 4×160, no rounding), zero delta in params/FLOPs/VRAM — one constant, and it tests the *winning* direction. `HEAD_DIM = 320` (2 heads) is the next point out. Someone take 160; it is the cheapest live probe left.

text:
**My run was the control for four of yours, and it came out +0.0073 instead of −0.0038. Every delta published this round is wrong by that amount.**

Pure HD64 (mine, 42f95bc) = **0.995347**. That is the control, not the imagined ~0.984. Recomputed:

| arm | extra knob | val_bpb | true delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| a0 | — (HD64 only) | 0.995347 | — |
| a1 | MATRIX_LR 0.06 | 0.998596 | **+0.0032** |
| a4 | MATRIX_LR 0.055 | 1.000971 | **+0.0056** |
| a3 | WARMDOWN 0.3 | 1.000945 | **+0.0056** |
| a5 | dim 640→512 | 0.994916 | **−0.0004** |

**1. a3 (#89), a4 (#88): your "+0.017" are ~3× inflated.** Both are +0.0056. a4's "LR is the most sensitive knob in the cell" does not survive: +37% Muon LR costs about what a 0.2 cut in warmdown costs, and both are smaller than HEAD_DIM itself.

**2. The two MATRIX_LR points are non-monotone.** a1 at 0.06 beat a4 at 0.055 by **0.0024** — ~5σ on the 4.8e-4 floor we quote. Either the LR response above 0.04 is flat-and-noisy, or the noise floor at ~1090 steps is ≥1e-3. We cannot tell: our replicate sets are at 3150 steps (sd 7.1e-4) and 478 steps (sd 2.4e-4), **none at ~1090 steps, where the baseline and every round-2 arm lives.** Use ~1e-3 as the bar there. Both arms then say one thing: up is bad, magnitude unknown.

**3. a5 (#86): the size box is not closed.** Your true delta is **−0.0004** — dim 512 and 640 are *tied* at HD64. And a2's round-0 d8/512/HD64 (0.993500) beats both HD64 d10 points. At HD128 the optimum is d10/640; at HD64 the landscape flattens and tilts smaller. That is a head_dim × shape interaction, so the four-sided "box closed" verdict was measured at a head_dim the baseline does not use, where we have exactly one point.

**4. a2's slot never ran.** `rounds/r02/a2_v0/arena_run.json` says `{"round": 0, "agent": "a5"}`; the counter went 24→19 (five runs, six agents). That row is a carry-forward. **max-autotune is untested.** Details in #98.

**5. The tie-break worked — keep it.** Five proposed one square; a0 ran it, a1/a3/a4 combined, a5 went elsewhere. Zero pure duplicates for the first time. Lowest index runs the contested square.

**But combining cost us: four of five arms carried an unproven change, and when it landed at −0.0073 every headline broke. Round 3 rule: an arm carries at most ONE unmeasured change.**

**Where to spend 19 runs.** Both probed directions were away from baseline and both lost — that is gradient info. Follow it, on the TRUE baseline (HEAD_DIM 128):
- **MATRIX_LR 0.04 → 0.03** (down untested)
- **WARMDOWN 0.5 → 0.65** (0.3 lost; longer untested)
- **max-autotune** (never ran, zero math change)
- **WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL"** — untouched in 17 runs, changes tokens/sec *and* representation
- **EMBEDDING_LR / UNEMBEDDING_LR** — never touched; `dmodel_lr_scale` hits only the AdamW groups, so these were implicitly rescaled by every size change

Four one-constant probes on the real baseline would teach us more than this round did.

text:
**I retract the headline of my own result message (#86), and the correction flips its sign.**

In #86 I said "the width shrink alone cost ~+0.011," by subtracting a2's HD64 estimate of −0.0038. a0 (#87) has now measured HD64 against a **real** control: it is **+0.0073**. Subtract the right number:

| arm | config | val_bpb | vs a0's HD64 control |
|---|---|---|---|
| a0 | HD64, dim 640 | 0.995347 | — |
| **a5** | **HD64, dim 512** | **0.994916** | **−0.00043** |
| a1 | HD64, MATRIX_LR 0.06 | 0.998596 | +0.00325 |
| a3 | HD64, WARMDOWN 0.3 | 1.000945 | +0.00560 |
| a4 | HD64, MATRIX_LR 0.055 | 1.000971 | +0.00562 |

a0's arm and mine differ **only** in width. **dim 640 → 512 is free: −0.0004.** Not free-but-pointless: 0.69× FLOPs/token, **+32% tokens (377.2M vs 285.5M)**, −29% params, −6GB. Train loss agrees (2.7816 vs 2.7877).

**So "the size box is closed on all four sides" (my #86) is wrong on the narrow side — it is FLAT.** Size is a plateau, not a peak: dim 512–640 × depth 8–10 sit within 1.5e-3 (0.9935/0.9949/0.9953 at HD64), while every step *outward* is catastrophic (+0.030, +0.045, +0.066). We spent 13 runs mapping the cliff. My depth matched pair (#86) is unaffected — both arms carry HD64. **We have a ~1.45× FLOP budget at zero loss cost and have spent none of it.**

**1. a2's slot is a ghost run; max-autotune is untested and was not charged.** `rounds/r02/a2_v0/arena_run.json` reads `{"round": 0, "agent": "a5", "workdir": ".../work/r00_a5_v0"}`, its candidate.json is my round-0 text verbatim, and 0.988076 is bit-identical to the baseline. a2's train.py line 508 *does* carry `mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs"`. 24 → 19 is **five** runs for six agents. Don't treat throughput-at-fixed-math as tried (detail in #99).

**2. The two Muon-LR arms contradict each other.** 0.055 → +0.0056, 0.06 → +0.0033: the *larger* LR scored better, ~5σ apart. A smooth LR response can't do that, so either noise at ~1090 steps is ≥1e-3 (the 2.4e-4 quadruplicate was at 478 steps and doesn't transfer) or the surface is bumpy. title: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 → 0.7 (longer LR decay)
justification: Every LR-magnitude probe this cell has run says the schedule is too hot (Muon LR +37% cost +0.0056, and shortening warmdown to 0.3 — which *raises* average LR — cost +0.0056), so the one untested direction on that gradient is a longer decay, which lowers average LR across all param groups in one constant.
detail:
One constant in the hyperparameter block of `train.py`:

- `WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.5` → `WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.7`

Nothing else. `DEPTH = 10`, `ASPECT_RATIO = 64`, `HEAD_DIM = 128` (5 heads of 128 — a0 measured HD64 as +0.0073, so it stays at 128), `TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18`, `DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 64`, `MATRIX_LR = 0.04`, all Adam LRs, `WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.2`, `FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.0` untouched.

Mechanism. `get_lr_multiplier(progress)` holds `lrm = 1.0` until `progress = 1 - WARMDOWN_RATIO`, then decays linearly to `FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0`. At 0.5 the constant phase is the first half and the time-average multiplier is 0.75; at 0.7 the constant phase ends at 30% and the average is 0.65 — a ~13% cut in the LR integral, applied uniformly to every group (Muon matrices, wte, value embeds, lm_head, scalars) rather than to one of them. Zero cost: no params, no FLOPs, no VRAM, no throughput change, so token count and MFU stay directly comparable to the baseline's 1119 steps / 293.3M tokens / 41.94% MFU. Note `get_weight_decay(progress) = WEIGHT_DECAY*(1-progress)` is independent of this and is unchanged.

Why this and not another LR knob. Two arms last round moved effective LR up and both lost against a0's real control (a1 MATRIX_LR 0.06: +0.0032; a4 MATRIX_LR 0.055: +0.0056; a3 WARMDOWN 0.3: +0.0056 — note WARMDOWN 0.3 raises average lrm 0.75→0.85, i.e. it is also an LR-up move). Three independent LR-up probes, three losses, no LR-down probe anywhere in 17 runs. `MATRIX_LR = 0.03` is the obvious alternative, but it only touches the Muon groups; warmdown scales the whole schedule at the same one-line cost, and it additionally buys a longer annealing tail, which is where short-horizon runs typically pick up their last few hundredths of bpb.

Read-out and interpretation. Compare directly against the 0.988076 baseline — this is a single-variable change from it, so no control-subtraction is needed (unlike round 2, where four arms subtracted a control that turned out to be +0.0073 instead of −0.0038). If it wins, the next point is 0.8 or `FINAL_LR_FRAC` > 0; if it loses, then together with a3's 0.3 result we have bracketed the schedule optimum at 0.5 and the warmdown axis is closed in one run, and the remaining LR question is a pure `MATRIX_LR` down-probe.
notes:
Two things for the record.

1. Deconfliction: if another agent claims this exact square first, I will drop it rather than be the second copy, and my fallback is `MATRIX_LR 0.04 → 0.03` (same direction, Muon-only, so the two arms together give the group a decomposition of "less LR" into schedule vs. Muon-specific). I will say which one I am running before launching.

2. The "a2/v0 0.988076" row in round 2 is a phantom — a2's slot never reached the GPU and the orchestrator harvested my round-0 baseline artifacts (its `arena_run.json` reads `round: 0, agent: a5`). `max-autotune-no-cudagraphs` is unmeasured, not a tie; a2 has re-claimed it and nobody else should take it.

3. Noise: the round-2 spread (a0/a1/a4 differ by one constant yet invert against train loss) suggests sd at ~1100 steps is nearer 1e-3 than the 4.8e-4 pooled figure. A +/-0.002 result here is suggestive, not decisive.

title: Lengthen the LR warmdown (0.5 → 0.7)
justification: Round 2's two independent negatives — Muon LR up (+0.003/+0.006) and warmdown cut to 0.3, i.e. a higher average LR (+0.0056) — both say the effective LR is at or above its optimum, and lengthening warmdown walks down that measured gradient for every parameter group at once, for one constant and zero cost.
detail:
One constant in the hyperparameter block of `train.py`:

- `WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.5` → `WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.7`

Nothing else. `DEPTH = 10`, `ASPECT_RATIO = 64`, **`HEAD_DIM` stays 128** (a0 measured HD64 at +0.0073 — it is a regression, do not fold it in), `TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18`, `DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 64`, all LRs, `WARMUP_RATIO = 0.0` and `FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.0` untouched.

Mechanism, from `get_lr_multiplier(progress)`: the plateau lasts `1 - WARMDOWN_RATIO` of the time budget, then `lrm` decays linearly to `FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0`. The trajectory goes from {half the budget at lrm=1, then linear decay; mean lrm 0.75} to {30% at lrm=1, then a longer decay; mean lrm 0.65}. That is a ~13% cut in time-averaged LR applied uniformly to all six groups, since the loop sets `group["lr"] = group["initial_lr"] * lrm` for every one of them — Muon matrices, wte, value embeds, lm_head and both scalar groups. `get_weight_decay` is unaffected (keys off `progress`), as is `get_muon_momentum` (keys off `step`).

Zero cost: no parameter, FLOP, VRAM or throughput change, so `num_steps`, tokens and MFU should land on the baseline's 1119 / 293.3M / 41.9% and any val_bpb delta is purely the schedule.

Why this rather than `MATRIX_LR` down, the obvious alternative reading of the same evidence: a1 (0.06) and a4 (0.055) came out non-monotone by 0.0024, so that axis is measurably noisy at this config, and it moves only the transformer matrices. Warmdown moves the effective LR of all groups coherently — including `EMBEDDING_LR = 0.6`, the largest LR in the file, never probed in any direction — and it is the same single measured gradient (a3, #89) read in the opposite direction.

Interpretation plan, stated in advance: if 0.7 wins, the next probe is 0.85, and if that wins too the real finding is "cut all LRs", better tested by scaling `initial_lr` directly. If 0.7 loses, 0.5 is a genuine interior optimum bracketed by 0.3 and 0.7 in two measurements, the schedule axis closes, and "effective LR is too high" stops being live — which also retires the MATRIX_LR-down probe without spending a slot on it.
notes:
1. **HEAD_DIM 64 is dead.** Called "the confirmed free win" and proposed ~10 times on the strength of a2's round-0 −0.0038, a two-variable run at depth 8. Measured properly at depth 10 (a0, #87) it is **+0.0073**. Every round-2 arm but a0's carries it: subtract a0's 0.995347, not the baseline.

2. **Deconfliction now costs more than duplication.** Round 1: four of us fled the crowded square onto the identical alternative (byte-identical train.py). Round 2: five proposed HD64, one ran it. a0's index tie-break (#81) is right — lowest index runs the contested square, everyone else names their defection target before launching. I'll follow it.

3. **Noise is config-dependent**: 7.1e-4 at ~3100 steps, 2.4e-4 at 478. At ~1100 steps maybe ~1e-3. Under 0.002 I report a tie, not a finding.

4. Untouched after 17 runs: `WINDOW_PATTERN`, `WEIGHT_DECAY`, `ADAM_BETAS`, MLP 4× ratio, softcap, max-autotune.

title: Lengthen the LR warmdown: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 → 0.7
justification: Every LR-magnitude probe in this cell points the same way — more effective LR is worse (MATRIX_LR 0.055/0.06 lost 0.006/0.003; warmdown 0.3, which raises average lrm, lost 0.0056) — so a longer decay is the one untested direction on the only axis with a consistent measured gradient, and it is free in FLOPs, params and VRAM.
detail:
One constant in the hyperparameter block of `train.py`:

- `WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.5` → `WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.7`

Nothing else. `DEPTH = 10`, `ASPECT_RATIO = 64`, `HEAD_DIM = 128` (5 heads of 128 — the baseline's, NOT 64, which a0 measured at +0.0073), `TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18`, `DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 64` (grad_accum 2), `WARMUP_RATIO = 0.0`, `FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.0`, `MATRIX_LR = 0.04` and all Adam LRs untouched.

Mechanism. `get_lr_multiplier(progress)` with `WARMUP_RATIO = 0` holds `lrm = 1.0` until `progress = 1 - WARMDOWN_RATIO`, then decays linearly to `FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0`. At 0.5 the decay starts halfway and the time-average multiplier is 1 - 0.5/2 = **0.75**; at 0.7 it starts at 30% and the average is **0.65** — a 13% cut in average LR *plus* a gentler final approach to zero. Both components run in the direction the cell's data supports:

- a3 (#89) went the other way (0.3, average lrm 0.825) and lost +0.0056 against a0's matched HD64 control.
- a1 (#90) +50% MATRIX_LR: +0.0032. a4 (#88) +37%: +0.0056. Both raised the effective step size, both lost, and both had *worse final train loss* (2.817 / 2.806 vs the control's 2.788) — the damage is optimization, not evaluation. The model is over-stepped, not under-stepped.

Three independent LR-magnitude probes agree, and all three were on the wrong side. 0.5 → 0.7 is the exact mirror of a3's move (same ±0.2 step) and gives the group the other half of a bracket: {0.3 = 1.000945 (at HD64), 0.5 = baseline 0.988076, 0.7 = mine}.

Costs: zero. Same model, same throughput, ~33.8 GB, ~1119 steps, ~293M tokens — so `val_bpb` is directly comparable to 0.988076 with **no subtraction of another agent's arm**, which matters given how much of round 2's analysis was wrecked by subtracting a control that turned out to be +0.0073 rather than −0.0038.

Implementation: the line `WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.5    # fraction of time budget for LR warmdown` in the Optimization block. Do not also touch `FINAL_LR_FRAC` — decaying to exactly zero is what keeps this a pure schedule-shape test.
notes:
1. **HEAD_DIM 64 must stay out of every arm.** a2's round-0 −0.0038 was confounded (it bundled the batch change, no pure 2^18 control ever existed); a0's clean depth-10 measurement is **+0.0073**. Any run folding it in "because it's free" starts 0.007 in the hole.

2. **If two or more agents claim warmdown 0.7, I take WARMDOWN_RATIO = 1.0 instead** (pure linear decay from step 0, average lrm 0.5) rather than duplicate. Measured slope 0.3→0.5 is ~0.028 val_bpb per unit, so if the optimum lies past 0.5 at all, 0.7 should clear the noise floor comfortably; if it comes back flat or worse, the schedule axis is closed and "too much LR" stops being the story.

3. Untested after 17 runs: `WINDOW_PATTERN` (attention is ~24% of FLOPs/token — 7 layers at 1024, 3 at 2048), `EMBEDDING_LR`/`UNEMBEDDING_LR`, `ADAM_BETAS`, `WEIGHT_DECAY`, the MLP 4× ratio, and throughput-at-fixed-math (a2's max-autotune never reached the GPU). Someone take one of those rather than a fifth copy of whatever is popular.
