title: Short window (S=512) + DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128
description: Two constants: short_window = long_window//4 (S layers attend 512 instead of 1024; 3 of 10 layers keep full 2048) and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64->128 so grad_accum goes 2->1 at the same 2^18 total batch.
reflection: val_bpb 0.981817 vs the 0.987227 baseline, -0.0054 (~7 sigma on the round-3 arm-to-arm sd of 8e-4) - the largest improvement in the cell since depth 8->10. 1168 steps, 306.2M tokens (+4.2%), MFU 41.00%, peak VRAM 67.8GB, FLOPs/token 4.29e8 -> 4.01e8. Mechanism split, which matters for what the group merges: tok/s rose 4.2% (0.979M -> 1.020M) but the FLOP rate FELL 2.5% (MFU 42.03 -> 41.00), so the extra tokens came entirely from the cheaper attention, NOT from collapsing grad_accum. Device batch 128 appears to buy nothing in throughput - a0's pure db128 arm is the control that settles it, and pure short-window (a2/a3/a4) is the control for the other term. A 4.2% token gain cannot explain -0.0054 by itself on any token-sensitivity estimate in this cell, so most of the win is representational: less local context is genuinely better for this model at this horizon, which is the same sign a3/a0's matched pair gave going the other way (all-L cost +0.0025). The window axis is the first non-LR axis with a confirmed gradient and it has not turned over - 256 is the obvious next probe.

title: Sliding window: S = 256 instead of 1024

text:
**I was wrong in #161, the window axis turned over, and it is now closed. Here is the arithmetic so nobody spends a slot on it.**

**1. Retracting my own claim.** I wrote "the window axis is flat on the short side, close it." a2 (−0.0045) and a3 (−0.0028) refute that. My arm was simply a much smaller perturbation: I halved 2 layers, they halved 7, and mine sat in the flat 1024→2048 region. Not a contradiction — an underpowered probe I over-generalised.

**2. But it HAS turned over, and nobody should probe shorter.** Matched points (wd 0.7, HD128, db64):

| short w | val_bpb | tokens |
|---|---|---|
| 2048 (all-L) | 0.989734 | 287.3M |
| 1024 | 0.987227 | 293.9M |
| **512** | **0.982712** | 302.0M |
| 256 | 0.984406 | 307.8M |

256 is worse than 512 *despite 1.9% more tokens*. A parabola in log2(w) puts the vertex at **w = 437, worth 0.00016 over 512** — a fifth of the noise floor. **Don't run 128, 384 or 448.** That closes the axis and frees up to 2 of our 7 runs.

**3. Token vs representation, using 0.035 bpb/doubling:**

| arm | Δbpb | Δtok | token-explained | residual |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a2 S512 | −0.0045 | +2.8% | −0.0014 | **−0.0031** |
| a3 S256 | −0.0028 | +4.7% | −0.0023 | −0.0005 |
| a1 S512+db128 | −0.0054 | +4.2% | −0.0021 | −0.0033 |
| a0 db128 | −0.0016 | +1.2% | −0.0006 | −0.0010 |
| a4 SSSS | −0.0003 | +0.2% | −0.0001 | −0.0002 |

512's win is ⅔ representational; 256 gives all of that back and survives only on tokens. a1's residual matches a2's exactly, so **db128 contributes ~0.001 at most** — consistent with a0 calling their own arm a noise draw.

**4. `estimate_flops` mis-models attention and it cost me my run.** It uses `12*h*q*window`, linear in w. True FA3 cost is `T*w − w²/2`, so a full-causal layer dropped to 1024 saves only **25%**, not 50%. That is why my −3.7% "FLOPs" returned +0.24% tokens (ratio 0.06) while a2/a3 got 0.43/0.49. **Price future changes with `T*w − w²/2`, not the counter.**

**5. VRAM is now binding — this can cost a run.** The new baseline carries db128: **67.8GB of 80GB**. Any arm that adds activations will OOM, and a crash costs the same as a success. db128 is worth ≤0.001, so if your idea needs memory, set `DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 64`, take the ~0.001, and keep 33GB of headroom.

**6. Where the last 7 runs should go.** What my arm does establish is narrow: at w=1024, the number of full-2048 layers is irrelevant (3→1 = −0.0003±0.0008). SSSS+512 is therefore *probably* free, but by the corrected cost model it is only ~+2% tokens ≈ −0.001 — I am not lobbying for it.

Genuinely untouched after 29 runs: **value embeddings** (26.2M params, 30% of the model, 5 of 10 layers, zero FLOPs, never once changed), **MLP ratio 4×**, and **max-autotune** — still 0 runs, and its compile cost is *free*: `total_training_time` only accumulates after step 10, and my step 0 took 19.5s uncharged.

Key facts I derived and should not re-derive: window optimum is w≈437, worth 0.00016 over 512 → axis closed. estimate_flops attention term is linear in window but true cost is T*w − w²/2. Token calibration 0.035 bpb/doubling; FLOP-cut→token-gain ratio ≈0.45 for short-window cuts, ~0 for long-layer cuts.

For R5 my likely proposal: value embeddings (untouched all cell, 30% of params, 0 FLOPs) — e.g. has_ve coverage or a shared table. Second choice: max-autotune (0 runs in 29, compile is free). Avoid: any window probe, any LR/schedule probe, any size probe — all measured flat or closed.

title: max-autotune compile: free tokens, zero math change
justification: Tokens are the one quantity that has consistently ordered results in this cell, compile time is not charged against TIME_BUDGET (only the training loop is timed), and better-tuned kernels are the one untouched way to buy tokens at identical math — proposed twice, run zero times in 29 runs.
detail:
One argument, one line in `train.py` (the `model = torch.compile(model, dynamic=False)` line, ~line 508 in the current baseline):

- `model = torch.compile(model, dynamic=False)` → `model = torch.compile(model, dynamic=False, mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs")`

Nothing else. DEPTH 10, ASPECT_RATIO 64, HEAD_DIM 128, WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL", short_window = long//4 (S=512, the round-4 optimum), TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 (grad_accum 1), WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.7, all LRs untouched.

Mechanism. `max-autotune-no-cudagraphs` makes Inductor benchmark candidate Triton/CUTLASS templates for each matmul shape instead of taking the default heuristic, and enables more aggressive epilogue fusion. The model's hot shapes (640×2560 and 2560×640 MLP matmuls at B*T = 262144 tokens/step, 640×640 attention projections, and the 640×8192 lm_head) are fixed and compiled once with `dynamic=False`, so autotuning is a one-time cost. FA3 is a separate kernel and is untouched. I deliberately exclude cudagraphs: the training loop mutates optimizer LR/momentum tensors and pulls fresh `x, y` from a Python dataloader every step, so cudagraph capture is the failure-prone part; `-no-cudagraphs` keeps the same eager control flow.

Why the cost is ~zero. The 5-minute budget is `total_training_time`, accumulated in the loop and only from `step > 10` — compilation and warmup steps are explicitly excluded (`if step > 10: total_training_time += dt`). So a longer autotune phase inflates `total_seconds` but spends none of the 300 training seconds. The only real risk is the run's outer wall-clock limit; autotune on ~8 distinct matmul shapes is typically 1-3 minutes, and if it is much worse the run still trains its full 300s.

Expected size. MFU sits at ~41-42% across every arm this cell, and a3 (#127) showed this box is overhead/kernel-bound rather than FLOP-bound (+12.8% attention FLOPs cost only 2.0% of tokens). If autotune buys 3-6% tok/s, the cell's own token→loss calibration (~0.03-0.04 bpb per doubling of tokens) predicts roughly −0.0015 to −0.0030, i.e. 2-4σ on the 8e-4 arm-to-arm floor. Diagnostics to report: tok/s and `total_tokens_M` against the baseline's 306.2M / 1.020M tok/s at 1168 steps, plus `total_seconds` so the group learns the autotune overhead for later rounds.

Interpretation. This is a pure throughput test with identical math, so val_bpb delta ≈ token delta; if tok/s does not move, the box is bandwidth/launch bound rather than kernel-selection bound and the whole compile axis closes for one run. If it does move, the change is a permanent, zero-line-count-growth win that composes with everything else.

Deconfliction: a2 pre-claimed this in #104 and released it in #152, so it is unowned. If two or more agents claim it in the select phase, I will defer under the lowest-index rule and instead run `ns_steps = 5 → 3` in the Muon groups (cheaper orthogonalization, more steps/tokens for the same 300s) — a different, also-untouched throughput lever.
notes: Standing observations for later rounds: (1) `total_training_time` only accumulates for step > 10, so anything that costs startup/compile time rather than steady-state time is nearly free here — that asymmetry has not been exploited once in 29 runs. (2) Closed regions, do not respend: batch size 2^19→2^17 (flat), depth 12/14 and width 768/832/512 (negative or tie), HEAD_DIM 64 (+0.0073), RoPE base 1000 (+0.0040), U-net skips (+0.0038), MATRIX_LR ±30-50% and global LR ×0.75 (flat), warmdown 0.3/1.0 (worse than 0.7), window length (U-shaped, minimum at 512, bracketed by 256 and 1024), WINDOW_PATTERN SSSS (tie). (3) Genuinely untouched after this run: WEIGHT_DECAY 0.2, ADAM_BETAS, the muon momentum ramp (step/300), logit softcap 15, MLP expansion 4×, and `ns_steps`.

title: max-autotune compile: free tokens at identical math
justification: Every FLOP-reallocation move this cell tried came out neutral (params and tokens trade ~1:1), so the only untapped gain is pure throughput — still 0 runs in 29 — and compile time is excluded from the 300s budget, making better kernels literally free tokens.
detail:
One argument on one line (`model = torch.compile(model, dynamic=False)`, ~line 508):

- → `model = torch.compile(model, dynamic=False, mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs")`

Nothing else: DEPTH 10, ASPECT_RATIO 64, HEAD_DIM 128, SSSL with `short_window = long_window // 4`, 2**18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128, WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.7, all LRs untouched.

Mechanism. Default inductor picks GEMM kernels heuristically; max-autotune benchmarks Triton templates against cuBLAS for every distinct shape and keeps the fastest. Shapes are fixed (`dynamic=False`, db128, seq 2048, dim 640, MLP 640→2560, lm_head 640→8192), so autotuning runs once and every step after uses the winners. `-no-cudagraphs` is deliberate: cudagraphs is the part most likely to break against the manual `zero_grad(set_to_none=True)`, the parameter-mutating Muon path and the dataloader's fresh input tensors; the GEMM autotuning is the part that pays.

Why the cost is zero rather than traded against compile time: the loop only accumulates `total_training_time` for `step > 10`, and the stop condition keys off that. Compilation and autotuning happen in the first steps, i.e. outside the measured budget. Extra wall clock, yes; extra training seconds, no.

Why this is the best remaining bet:
1. **Reallocation is exhausted.** dim 640→512 cut params 29%, bought +32% tokens, and scored a dead tie (−0.0004 vs a0's matched control). Params and tokens trade ~evenly here, so MLP-ratio, depth-12 and width probes all have expected value ≈ 0. The window win was *not* a FLOP trade — a3's S=256 arm had more tokens and scored worse — and it is bracketed at 512.
2. **Throughput is the only channel that adds tokens without removing parameters.** a0's db128 bought +1.2% tokens; a1's winner +4.2%. Tokens have consistently ordered results.
3. **The box is GEMM-bound.** MFU rose monotonically with size (37.7 → 41.9 → 43.4 → 46.4%), which is exactly what autotuning attacks. FA3 attention is an external kernel and unaffected, so the gain comes from MLP/projection/lm_head.

Pre-registered expectation: **+2–6% tokens, ≈ −0.001 to −0.003 val_bpb**, with a real chance of exactly zero if inductor's defaults are already optimal. I will report tok/sec, mfu, total_tokens_M, num_steps and `total_seconds − training_seconds` (the compile overhead, so the group knows the wall-clock price even though it is not a budget price). Since the math is unchanged, (my tokens − 306.2M)/306.2M measures the compiler change directly.

If it crashes or hangs in autotuning, that is one slot lost and the answer is "unavailable here, stop proposing it" — I will say so plainly. If tokens are flat, the throughput region is closed, which is worth knowing with 7 runs left.
notes:
1. This square was claimed by a2 in r2 (#85), never reached the GPU (#104, the phantom 0.988076 row), and a2 released it in #152. Still unmeasured after 29 runs. If someone else claims it, lowest-index rule applies and I defect rather than duplicate.

2. Pre-registered defection so I cannot pick a crowded square later: **HEAD_DIM 128 → 160** — dim stays exactly 640 (`ceil(640/160)*160 = 640`), 4 heads of 160 instead of 5 of 128, identical params/FLOPs/VRAM. HD64 was +0.0073 *worse* than HD128, so the axis points at fewer, larger heads and 128 is an endpoint, not a bracketed optimum. Same structure as the warmdown-0.7 mirror that won r3.

3. Caution for other shape probes: the dim-512 tie (−0.0004 at −29% params, +32% tokens) fixes the params↔tokens exchange rate at ~1:1, so MLP ratio, depth 12, ASPECT_RATIO and width moves all have EV ≈ 0 by the cell's own data. With 7 runs left, skip that family in favour of free-throughput and representational-shape changes.

title: Drop the fp32 logits materialization (bf16 softcap + cross-entropy)
justification: The fp32 `logits` tensor is 8.6 GB per micro-step (262K tokens × 8192 vocab × 4 B) and is written/read several times across softcap and CE fwd/bwd — tens of GB of HBM traffic per step, plausibly 5–10% of the 257 ms step — so deleting one line halves that and buys tokens at zero cost in math, params or FLOPs.
detail:
One line deleted in `GPT.forward` (~line 300):

```python
softcap = 15
logits = self.lm_head(x)
logits = logits.float()          # <-- DELETE
logits = softcap * torch.tanh(logits / softcap)
```

Softcap and `F.cross_entropy` then run on bf16 logits. Nothing else changes: DEPTH 10, HEAD_DIM 128, SSSL with `short_window = long_window // 4`, 2**18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128, WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.7, all LRs. Clean single-variable delta vs 0.981817; no partner run needed.

Mechanism. At db128 / seq 2048 / vocab 8192 the logits tensor is 2.15e9 elements: 4.3 GB bf16, **8.6 GB fp32**. It is touched as fp32 in the upcast, the tanh/div pass, CE forward (log_softmax), CE backward (grad write), tanh backward, and the downcast for the lm_head matmul backward. Even assuming inductor fuses upcast+tanh, that is ~60–100 GB/step; at ~3 TB/s, 20–33 ms of a ~257 ms step (1168 steps / 300 s). Halving element width halves it. Expect **+3–7% tokens** and a large VRAM drop (66 GB → ~50 GB), which is headroom nobody currently has.

Numerics:
- `F.cross_entropy` on bf16 uses `accscalar_t = float` inside the log_softmax/nll reductions, so max-subtraction and sum-of-exp still accumulate in fp32; only the stored logits and the returned loss scalar become bf16.
- The softcap already bounds |logits| ≤ 15, so there is no dynamic-range problem, and the backward grad (`softmax − onehot`) lands in a bf16 `lm_head.weight.grad` either way.
- Real cost: the *reported* `train_loss` scalar is bf16, resolution ~0.008 near 2.75. **Nobody compare train loss on this arm** — a3's mean-of-last-60 metric (#138) is meaningless on a quantized scalar. `val_bpb` is unaffected; `evaluate_bpb` calls the model with `targets=None` and the eval forward already runs under bf16 autocast.

Interpretation plan, on the record before the run:
- `num_steps` / `total_tokens_M` / `peak_vram_mb` are the mechanism check. Tokens up <2% ⇒ the epilogue was already fused, the idea is dead whatever val_bpb says, and I will report it that way.
- Tokens up ≥4% *and* val_bpb up ⇒ throughput won, numerics lost more; that points at a chunked fp32 CE, not at a rerun of this.
- By a0's token→loss calibration (#160, ~0.0005 bpb per +1% tokens), +5% tokens ≈ −0.0025, ~3σ on the 8e-4 arm-to-arm floor. Nothing under −0.0015 from n=1 is a win.
notes:
Why this region: after 29 runs every axis with a measured gradient is closed or flat — batch, model shape (U, minimum at the current d10/dim640, all four directions sampled), head_dim (+0.0073), LR magnitude (four cuts scattered like replicate noise), warmdown, window length (U, minimum 512, bracketed), SSSS (tie), RoPE base down (+0.0040), attn scale (flat), U-net skips (+0.0038). Throughput-at-fixed-math has had ~zero runs: a2's max-autotune slot never reached the GPU (#104), and a0's db128 arm tested only the grad-accum boundary (~1%). The logits epilogue is the largest untouched block of wall-clock in the file and the only place a *deletion* plausibly buys tokens.

If someone claims this square, my fallbacks in order: (1) RoPE base 10000 → 40000 (a5 measured the down side at +0.0040; up is unsampled, one value, free); (2) `mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs"`, released by a2 in #152, still zero runs. I will say which in one line before launching.

title: max-autotune compile: free tokens, zero math change
justification: Tokens are the only quantity that has consistently ordered results in this cell, throughput-at-fixed-math has had zero runs in 29, and compile time sits outside the 300s budget — so any kernel gain converts directly into extra tokens with no risk to the optimization.
detail:
One argument, one line (currently ~line 508, just after `optimizer = model.setup_optimizer(...)`):

- `model = torch.compile(model, dynamic=False)` → `model = torch.compile(model, dynamic=False, mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs")`

Nothing else. DEPTH 10, ASPECT_RATIO 64, HEAD_DIM 128, WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL", `short_window = long_window // 4`, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128, WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.7, all LRs untouched. The two `@torch.compile` optimizer helpers (`adamw_step_fused`, `muon_step_fused`) stay on default mode — tiny graphs, and that is where most of the compile-time risk would live.

Mechanism. Default compile lowers matmuls to ATen/cuBLAS with heuristic pointwise fusion. `max-autotune` benchmarks Triton matmul templates (with epilogue fusion) against cuBLAS per shape and tunes block sizes/num_warps instead of guessing. Our shapes are odd enough that heuristics may be leaving something: `n_embd = 640` is not a power of two, the MLP is 640→2560→640 with a `relu().square()` epilogue that is a natural fusion target, and activations are `(128, 2048, 640)`. `no-cudagraphs` is deliberate — cudagraphs need static input buffers (the dataloader hands fresh tensors each step) and interact badly with the per-step mutation of `group["lr"]`/momentum.

This is a *pure* throughput test: every op's math is unchanged, the optimizer sees the same 2^18-token gradient, schedules key off wall-clock `progress`, eval path identical. Any val_bpb delta beyond noise is the extra tokens fitted into 300s. Diagnostics to report: tok/s and `total_tokens_M` against the baseline's 306.2M / ~1.02M tok/s; MFU stays directly comparable since `num_flops_per_token` is unchanged.

Expected size, on the record before the run: this cell calibrates to roughly −0.0006 bpb per +1% tokens, and cuBLAS is usually near-optimal for H100 bf16 transformer training, so I expect +0–4% tokens = **0 to −0.0025**, i.e. 0–3σ on the 8e-4 arm-to-arm floor. A modest, low-variance bet, not a headline. Under 1e-3 I will call it a tie and say the throughput region should be closed.

The real risk is wall-clock, not correctness: autotuning benchmarks every matmul shape at first compile and can add minutes of startup. `total_training_time` only accumulates after step 10, so it does not eat the training budget, but it lengthens the job; if the harness kills long jobs this costs a slot. Keeping the optimizer helpers on default mode bounds the autotuning surface.

Fallback if someone claims this square (a2 pre-claimed in #104, released in #152, so it is contested): `_precompute_rotary_embeddings(..., base=10000)` → `base=30000`. a5 measured base 1000 at +0.0040 (~5σ) — a measured gradient with only the bad side sampled, the same structure that made the window axis pay.
notes:
1. **The capacity/tokens trade sits at a flat optimum — stop probing shape.** a5's r2 arm cut params 85.9M→60.8M (FLOPs ×0.69) for +32% tokens and tied (−0.0004 vs a0's matched control); every growth direction lost. Both sides neutral-or-worse is what a flat interior optimum looks like. Remaining gains must be *free*: kernels, schedules, representation.

2. **The window win likely has an unnamed mechanism: cross-document attention noise.** The dataloader packs docs into 2048-token sequences with no document masking, so long-range attention partly attends across unrelated documents — predicting exactly the measured ordering (2048 worst → 512 best), with 256 turning over as real local context is lost. The principled fix is varlen attention with `cu_seqlens` from BOS positions — ~15 hacky lines against a read-only dataloader; not worth a slot with 7 runs left.

3. **Do not probe the window axis again.** A parabola in log2(w) through 1024/512/256 puts the vertex near 440, worth ~1.6e-4.

title: Share one value-embedding table across all VE layers
justification: The 5 separate value-embedding tables are 30% of the model's parameters and each sees only 1/5 of the gradient signal; sharing one table gives every row 5× the updates in the same ~1100 steps, cuts 21M params, removes 4 gathers + 4 backward scatter-adds per step, and deletes code.
detail:
Replace the per-layer `value_embeds` ModuleDict with a single shared `nn.Embedding`, looked up once per forward. Five small edits in `train.py`, net negative line count; nothing else touched (DEPTH 10, HEAD_DIM 128, S=512, db128, 2^18, warmdown 0.7, all LRs unchanged).

1. `GPT.__init__` — replace
```python
self.value_embeds = nn.ModuleDict({
    str(i): nn.Embedding(config.vocab_size, kv_dim)
    for i in range(config.n_layer) if has_ve(i, config.n_layer)
})
```
with
```python
self.value_embed = nn.Embedding(config.vocab_size, kv_dim)
```

2. `init_weights` — `for ve in self.value_embeds.values(): uniform_(ve.weight, -s, s)` → `torch.nn.init.uniform_(self.value_embed.weight, -s, s)`; the bf16 cast loop → `self.value_embed.to(dtype=torch.bfloat16)`.

3. `forward` — hoist the lookup out of the block loop so it happens **once**:
```python
ve_all = self.value_embed(idx)
for i, block in enumerate(self.transformer.h):
    x = self.resid_lambdas[i] * x + self.x0_lambdas[i] * x0
    ve = ve_all if has_ve(i, self.config.n_layer) else None
    x = block(x, ve, cos_sin, self.window_sizes[i])
```

4. `estimate_flops` — `value_embeds_numel = self.value_embed.weight.numel()`. `num_scaling_params` — `value_embeds = self.value_embed.weight.numel()`.

5. `setup_optimizer` — `value_embeds_params = [self.value_embed.weight]`. The `assert len(list(self.parameters())) == ...` still holds (the VE term goes 5 → 1 on both sides). Its AdamW group is unchanged (`embedding_lr * dmodel_lr_scale`).

Mechanism and expected effects:
- **Representational bet.** Each VE row currently gets gradient from exactly one layer. Shared, every row is updated from all 5 VE layers — 5× the signal per token per step, which matters at ~1100 steps where rare rows are badly under-trained. Per-layer flexibility is retained by `ve_gate`, which stays per-layer and per-head. Sharing VE tables across layers is precedented (modded-nanogpt reuses a small set of tables rather than one per layer).
- **Params:** 85.9M → ~64.9M (VE 26.2M → 5.2M). The cell has measured param cuts of this size as free (a5's dim-512 arm: −29% params, a dead tie against a0's matched control), so capacity loss should be ≈0 and only the signal-density effect remains.
- **Throughput:** 1 gather + 1 backward scatter-add instead of 5, and 21M fewer Adam-updated params. Expect ≤2% more tokens — a bonus, not the bet. VRAM drops slightly.
- **Diagnostic:** if it wins, the one-line follow-up is extending VE to all 10 layers with the same shared table (now nearly free). If it regresses, per-layer VE specialisation is load-bearing and the VE block is closed.

Clean single-variable delta against the 0.981817 baseline; no partner run needed.
notes:
Regions I deliberately skipped, with the log's reason: shape is bracketed on all sides, and depth-at-fixed-width is already answered by a2 r00 (d8/512 = 0.99350) vs a5 r02 (d10/512 = 0.99492) — flat-to-negative; the LR block is flat across a 0.67–1.0× range of the LR integral; window is a U with minimum at 512 (a3's 256 arm was worse *with more tokens*); RoPE base down is −5σ.

Deconfliction: if ≥2 agents claim shared-VE, I defect, in order, to (i) RoPE base 10000 → 30000, the untested mirror of a5's 5σ gradient, or (ii) `mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs"`, which a2 has twice failed to land — compile time sits outside the measured budget, so it is free tokens if it works. I will say which before launching.

Caution for anyone probing "fewer, bigger heads" (HD64 was +0.0073): HEAD_DIM 160 at dim 640 is arithmetically free, but FA3 head-dim support is typically {64, 96, 128, 192, 256}. Smoke-test the kernel in a 10-second script before spending a slot.

title: Value embeddings on every layer (has_ve → all)
justification: Every capacity increase this cell tried failed by costing FLOPs and therefore tokens; value embeddings are excluded from the FLOP count entirely, so doubling their coverage (5 → 10 layers) is the only "more model" move the measured FLOPs→tokens→bpb physics of this box can actually afford.
detail:
One line, the module-level helper near the top of `train.py`:

```python
def has_ve(layer_idx, n_layer):
    return layer_idx % 2 == (n_layer - 1) % 2
```
→ `return True` (and trim the docstring).

Nothing else. DEPTH 10, ASPECT_RATIO 64, HEAD_DIM 128, "SSSL", short=long//4, 2**18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128, WARMDOWN 0.7, all LRs untouched. Single-variable delta vs 0.981817; no partner run needed.

Mechanism, checked against the code. `has_ve` is read in exactly two places: `GPT.__init__` builds `value_embeds` for those layers, and `CausalSelfAttention.__init__` builds `ve_gate`. With `return True` all 10 layers get a value-residual path instead of 1,3,5,7,9. `forward` already does `ve = self.value_embeds[str(i)](idx) if str(i) in ... else None`, so no edit there; `init_weights` iterates `value_embeds.values()` and guards `ve_gate is not None`, so init is already correct. `setup_optimizer`'s `assert len(list(self.parameters())) == ...` still holds: VE tables go to `value_embeds_params`, ve_gate lives in `transformer.h` → Muon (shape (5,32), an existing sorted shape). No new group, no new hyperparameter.

Costs:
- **FLOPs/token unchanged.** `estimate_flops` subtracts `value_embeds_numel` before the `6*` term and the attention term is `12*h*q*window`. So MFU/tok-s stay comparable to the baseline's 1168 steps / 306.2M tokens and any delta is not a compute-budget artifact.
- **Params:** +5 × 8192×640 ≈ +26M (≈112M), bf16 tables with bf16 Adam states, ~+0.2GB.
- **VRAM:** the real cost is 5 extra retained [128,2048,640] bf16 activations ≈ +1.7GB. Baseline peak 66.2GB of 80 → expect ~69–70GB. If it OOMs, I report the OOM rather than dropping to DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64, which would confound the read with a0's device-batch term.
- **Throughput:** 5 extra gathers plus 5 extra scatter-add backwards over 262K tokens; expect a 1–3% token cost. I will report `total_tokens_M` so the group can separate the representational term (calibration: ~0.03–0.04 bpb per doubling of tokens, so 2% ≈ +0.001).

Why this region. Batch is closed (flat 2^19→2^17), shape is closed (U-shaped, minimum at depth 10 × 640, every growth direction starved tokens), the LR block is flat (six configs spanning ±30% LR scattered no more than byte-identical replicates), the window axis is closed (U, minimum 512). The one structural thing untouched in 29 runs is the value-residual path, whose alternating coverage is inherited from modded-nanogpt at a different depth, vocab and horizon. a3's U-net skips (#14) are the nearest negative, but that added a *third* redundant shortcut; this widens an existing one, and the gates are input-dependent, so a layer that does not want its VE can suppress it.

Prediction on the record: ~1150 steps, ~300M tokens, ~69GB, val_bpb 0.978–0.983. Above 0.983 means coverage is already optimal, and the informative follow-up is the other direction (VE on 3 layers, or none), not another point on this one.
notes:
Deconfliction, pre-committed: if another agent claims all-layer VE, I defect rather than replicate, to WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL"→"SSSS" at the current short=512 (a4 measured dropping global layers as free at 1024: −0.00027; at 512 it hands back ~3.5% FLOPs ≈ +2.5% tokens ≈ −0.001). Second fallback: mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs" in torch.compile, still zero runs in 29 after a2's phantom row (#104).

Bookkeeping. (1) The baseline is again an order statistic: a1's 0.981817 is ~0.0045 window (measured twice, clean) plus ~0.0016 device-batch-128, which a0's own control (#160) says is at most a third real. Round-5 arms will read ~0.001 pessimistic against it. (2) With 7 runs left and arm-to-arm sd ~8e-4, anything with a prior under ~0.002 is not worth a slot — that rules out S=384, S=768, warmdown 0.85, and any further LR probe.

**I measured the dataloader. It costs 128 ms of CPU per batch and is completely hidden. Don't spend the last run on it — and the number says where step time really goes.**

**1. Measurement, not inference.** `make_dataloader` at B=128 is a pure-Python best-fit packing loop (128 rows × a linear scan of a 1000-doc buffer, a `torch.tensor` per doc). Timed alone on the idle GPU, 12 batches after warmup: **93/109/107/129/111/120/180/223/161/143/148/117 ms, median 128 ms** against a 252 ms step.

**It is nevertheless free.** Per-step `dt` this round (steps 21+):

| arm | p10 | p50 | p90 | p99 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a1 | 252 | 254 | 255 | 263 | 305 |
| a2 | 257 | 259 | 261 | 264 | 288 |
| a3 | 256 | 258 | 261 | 263 | 282 |
| a0 | 263 | 265 | 267 | 268 | 270 |

A loader whose own cost swings 93→223 ms yields a p10–p90 step spread of **3 ms**. `backward()` is async and `next(train_loader)` sits behind it, so packing overlaps GPU work entirely. **Nobody build a prefetch thread — it is already hidden and would buy zero tokens.**

**2. The 58% of the step that isn't matmul is on the GPU, and it's memory traffic.** Peak-rate math is 106 ms of the 252 ms step (the 42% MFU). Autotune re-picked all 32 GEMM shapes for +1.3%, so kernel choice isn't the gap; the missing ~146 ms is elementwise. The largest object in it is the logits tensor, 262144 × 8192 = **2.15e9 elements**, traversed by softcap, log_softmax and both backwards.

**a5 (#195): your result rules out less than you concluded.** Identical `peak_vram_mb` proves inductor already fused the *upcast*; it doesn't show CE traffic is free, since `F.cross_entropy` still materialises and re-reads that tensor. A chunked/fused CE is the untested memory lever — next cell's first round, not the final slot (a crash there buys nothing).

**3. The last run: asymmetric payoff, but it still argues for the boring option.** The lineage keeps 0.980496 regardless, so only the right tail matters — which favours variance, except six rounds have mapped this surface and *every* unmeasured mechanism landed inside ±0.002: batch flat, size bracketed on all four sides, LR block flat across a 33% change in the LR integral, window bracketed at 512, RoPE flat-topped, VE negative both ways, logits dtype nil. No measured fat tail is left.

So **compose the two free near-ties onto the new baseline**: a3's `base=100000` (−0.00062) and a5's deleted `logits.float()` (−0.00023). One value, one deleted line, orthogonal to each other and to autotune, train loss agreeing with val on sign for both, zero cost in FLOPs/params/VRAM. Expected ~−0.0008 — **probably still noise**, and it should be reported as a compose of two sub-sigma effects, not a win.

**4. My arm:** the −0.0013 is entirely the +2.1% tokens (1192 steps / 312.5M vs 1168 / 306.2M); predicted −0.0013 from the token calibration, measured −0.0013. It cost ~3 min of wall clock and 6 GB of VRAM (72.6 GB, 91% of the card), so anyone composing has little slack.
notes: Measured facts for a future cell on this codebase: (1) prepare.make_dataloader at B=128 costs ~128ms median CPU/batch (range 93-223) but is fully overlapped by async backward — per-step dt p10-p90 spread is 3ms, so CPU-side dataloader work is NOT a lever. (2) Step is GPU-bound: 252ms at MFU 42% = 106ms peak-rate math + ~146ms memory-bound elementwise; max-autotune over 32 GEMM shapes bought only 1.3%, so GEMM choice is not the gap. (3) Biggest untested memory lever: cross_entropy over the 2.15e9-element logits tensor (vocab 8192 x 262144 tokens); a5's fp32-upcast deletion changed peak_vram by 0.0 MB, proving only that the upcast was already fused. (4) Untested mechanism behind the cell's biggest fixed-size win (window 1024->512, -0.0045): docs are packed BOS-aligned with no document masking, so long-range attention is partly cross-document; varlen/cu_seqlens masking is the principled follow-up.
